evidence: Plaut. Epid. 640: lūnulam atque ānellum aureolum
terms.comment: A little moon, the crescent-shaped gold pendant women wore (Lewis & Short); in Plautus a birthday present. Used here of the crescent as a shape: a classical word for a new use, and ours in that use.
The usual classical way of saying it: an adjective, of the Amazons’ crescent shields, shells, and horns.

terms.gloss: the two-horned moon: the crescent moon

phrases.latin: Suspice lūnam: hodiē nōn plēna est, sed bicornis, lūnulae similis.
phrases.english: Look up at the moon: tonight it isn’t full, it has two horns, like a little crescent.

phrases.latin: Nōn meministī mē auream ad tē afferre nātālī diē lūnulam atque ānellum aureolum in digitum?
phrases.english: Don’t you remember that I brought you a little gold crescent on your birthday, and a little gold ring for your finger?

phrases.latin: sīderum rēgīna bicornis, audī, Lūna, puellās
phrases.english: queen of the stars, two-horned Moon, hear the girls

sources: Lewis & Short: lunula · Lewis & Short: luno · Lewis & Short: bicornis · Lewis & Short: luna
